correctness.rationale: Conditional row normalization and mean constraints give exactly r,s∈[0,1/4] and r+s=H=p−1/2, so all couplings are parameterized. Monotone one-dimensional W2 coupling of the discrete rows to their centered Gaussians has covariance g(t)=φ(Φ^{-1}(t))+φ(Φ^{-1}(t+1/2)); objective is constant−Rg(r)−g(s). g″ is strictly negative, g′(0+)=+∞, g′(1/4)=0; unique interior critical point follows by endpoint derivative signs. Derivative w.r.t. R positive. Mills ratio implies g′(t)∼√(2log(1/t)) at 0 and Taylor g′(1/4−t)=ct+O(t²); the three regimes follow separately with H relative to 1/4. I independently solved 13 parameter/scale cases, confirmed feasibility, stationarity, concavity and c≈6.293730161. The analytic proof, not finite R numerics, establishes the quantifiers.

final_claim: For the 2x3 mean-preserving atomic transport with Gaussian references N(-1/2,R^2) and N(1/2,1), unique interior minimizer has r+s=p-1/2 and Rg′(r)=g′(s). As R→∞: if p<3/4, log(1/s)/R²→g′(p−1/2)²/2; if p=3/4, Rs/√(2log R)→1/c; if p>3/4, R(1/4−r)→g′(p−3/4)/c, c=2/φ(Φ−1(3/4)).
limitations: Restricted to two initial and three terminal atoms and two centered Gaussian references
